correctness.rationale: The 12-block adjacency masks determine a symmetric connected simple graph. Every forcing set omits at most one vertex from a twin block; with at most one missing vertex per block, the quotient algorithm is equivalent to each permitted full-graph forcing move. Exhaustive evaluation of the 4096 quotient masks obtains 214,247,214 successful masks at three, four and five whites and corresponding exact weighted sums 680,678,690. For the expanded block of size 2+t the success indicator does not depend on t>=0; the exact slopes 112,64,68 give adjacent coefficients 690+68t,678+64t,680+112t and strict valleys 12+4t and 2+48t. An independently implemented full-vertex simulation exhausts 2^18 subsets and reproduces the complete polynomial, 105 edges and connectivity. No false inference about a global minimum is made.

value.rationale: A primary 2026 publication asks for the smallest order with nonunimodal ordinary zero-forcing polynomial. A subsequent explicit bound of 19 is improved to 18 with a complete self-contained graph and reproducible full polynomial. The new proof also establishes an infinite connected twin-expansion family, with exact affirmative coefficient-gap formulas at every size n>=18. This is a motivated improvement to an unknown natural minimum and a structural perpetuation mechanism, not an arbitrary polynomial calculation or reparameterization of the prior large-order family. It does not claim to settle the exact minimum.
